newsitem.title: USA: Medical Graphics sets broad restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Medical Graphics sets broad restructuring.

text.p: Medical Graphics Corp, a maker of cardiorespiratory diagnostic systems, said Wednesday it was taking several restructuring actions, including implementing a $7 million cost-cutting program that will result in elimination of more than 50 jobs; closing its Dusseldorf, Germany office; and resdesigning some products.
The company said it had negotiated the following arrangements to help strengthen its balance sheet, provide liquidity and improve cash flow:
-- a $4.1 million credit facility through Norwest Business Credit;
-- a $4.3 million vendor payment plan that has been accepted by 90 percent of its vendors.
Medical Graphics said it is tightening cost controls, improving working capital management and significantly lowering general and administrative expenses.

In addition, the company said it is spinning off and licensing its Asthma Treatment Centers of America business to a private party. "As a result, Medical Graphics will receive revenue from equipment sales," it said.

It also said it was completing negotiations with a number of alliance partners to sell other companies' products through its direct sales force and to extend the reach of its technology into new markets through alternate distribution agreements. The results of these negotiations will be announced shortly, Medical Graphics said.
Senior managers are included in the job cuts, it said.
The redesign of several of the company's pulmonary products is aimed at providing greater value to customers while decreasing Medical Graphics's costs, the company said.
The company said it had hired Deloitte & Touche LLP as its independent auditor.
